info.name: Multi-Vendor E-Commerce API
info.description: Real, implemented endpoints only (Phases 1-25). No Wallet/Commission, Promotion/Coupon, Review, Notification, or Audit endpoints exist yet -- their Prisma models exist but have no application layer. No real payment gateway is integrated (foundation only, no signature verification). ADMIN-only requests (Category create/update, Vendor verification/activation, Refund create) require adminAccessToken to be set manually, since no self-service admin-provisioning endpoint exists -- assign the ADMIN role to a seeded user directly via Prisma. RBAC demo permission-based requests similarly require manually-seeded Permission/RolePermission rows. IMPORTANT: Cart 'Add item to cart' requires the variant's parent Product, Vendor, AND the variant itself to all be ACTIVE -- a freshly-applied Vendor is PENDING by default, so run 04 Vendors > Update vendor verification status (twice: UNDER_REVIEW then VERIFIED) and Activate vendor BEFORE 11 Cart, or 'Add item to cart' returns 400. Suggested execution order: Auth -> Vendors (apply, then ADMIN verifies + activates) -> Shops -> Categories (ADMIN) -> Products (create, then update status to ACTIVE) -> Product Variants -> Inventory (restock) -> Product Images -> Cart -> Checkout -> Orders / Vendor Orders -> Payments -> Webhooks -> Refunds.

item.name: 00 Admin Setup
item.description:
Logs in as a pre-provisioned ADMIN-role test account and captures {{adminAccessToken}}, used by every ADMIN-only request elsewhere in this collection (vendor verification/activation, category create/update, refund creation, and the ADMIN-gated RBAC demo routes).

No self-service admin-provisioning endpoint exists in this API by design -- registering a user assigns NO role at all (src/auth/auth.service.ts), and Role/UserRole are separate tables (prisma/schema/identity-access.prisma) with no seed data beyond the three Role rows themselves (prisma/seed.ts). The ADMIN test account referenced by {{adminEmail}}/{{adminPassword}} must already exist and already hold the ADMIN role via a one-time, out-of-band UserRole assignment -- see docs/postman-testing.md 'Admin test provisioning'. This request only logs in; it cannot create that access itself.

item.name: 03 RBAC / Authorization Demo
item.description: Demonstration-only endpoints exercising AuthorizationGuard end to end (not real business endpoints). Role-based requests below work with any seeded ADMIN/VENDOR account. Permission-based requests (products:read, inventory:adjust) require Permission/RolePermission rows that are NOT seeded by prisma/seed.ts by design (see docs/database/identity-access.md) -- create them manually via Prisma Studio/direct DB access first, or expect 403.

request.description: Only PENDING->UNDER_REVIEW, UNDER_REVIEW->VERIFIED, PENDING/UNDER_REVIEW->REJECTED are accepted. Run this request three times (UNDER_REVIEW, then VERIFIED) before Activation below.

item.name: Update vendor verification status to VERIFIED (ADMIN)

request.description: Second, required step of the two-hop verification lifecycle (PENDING -> UNDER_REVIEW -> VERIFIED, src/vendors/vendors.service.ts ALLOWED_VERIFICATION_TRANSITIONS). Requires status=PENDING and verificationStatus=VERIFIED (run the verification request(s) above first).

item.name: Stream image (public if product is ACTIVE)

request.description: Publicly streamable with no token if the parent product is ACTIVE. For a DRAFT/INACTIVE/ARCHIVED product, remove the noauth override and use the owning vendor's (or an ADMIN's) accessToken instead.

The 11 Cart folder above deliberately exercises Remove/Clear too, which leaves the cart empty -- re-adding here is what actually gives Checkout below something to convert (verified live: without this, checkout genuinely 400s with "Your cart is empty or does not exist", CheckoutService's own real message, not a fabricated one).

item.name: Get my vendor order by id

request.description: Requires the caller to own this VendorOrder, or be ADMIN. Only the documented transitions are accepted: PENDING->CONFIRMED, CONFIRMED->PROCESSING, PROCESSING->READY_TO_SHIP, READY_TO_SHIP->SHIPPED, SHIPPED->DELIVERED, and PENDING/CONFIRMED->CANCELLED.

PaymentsService.retry only accepts a Payment whose status is FAILED (src/payments/payments.service.ts) -- a freshly created payment starts PENDING, so Retry below needs this webhook to run first (verified live: without it, Retry genuinely 409s with "payment is not retryable", not a fabricated response).

Note: like Restock/Adjust inventory, this @Post() route has no @HttpCode override, so it returns Nest's POST default, 201, not the 200 its own @ApiOkResponse Swagger decorator documents -- asserted here against the real, verified response.

item.name: 18 Security & Negative Tests
item.description: Negative/security-behavior checks that do NOT require an ADMIN account, so they run in every environment regardless of RBAC fixture availability. Each documents one specific, source-verified failure mode rather than a generic smoke check.

request.description: GET /api/auth/me is guarded by JwtAuthGuard (src/auth/auth.controller.ts). Calling it with no Authorization header at all must be rejected before any handler logic runs.

POST /api/categories requires @Roles('ADMIN') (src/catalog/categories/categories.controller.ts). {{accessToken}} here belongs to the plain customer registered in 02 Auth, who holds no roles at all -- AuthorizationGuard must reject this as 403, not 401 (the token itself is valid) and not 500.

A well-formed but non-existent UUID against GET /api/categories/:categoryId -- this route carries NO guard at all (src/catalog/categories/categories.controller.ts), so CategoriesService.findById's NotFoundException is the genuine, unmasked 404. (GET /api/products/:productId, by contrast, sits behind ProductOwnershipGuard, which fails closed with 403 for both 'not owned' and 'does not exist' -- see the next request -- so it cannot be used to demonstrate a bare 404.)
RegisterDto's @IsEmail() rejects this at the global ValidationPipe before AuthService.register ever runs.

Same authenticated user applying a second time. Vendor.userId is unique (1 User -> max 1 Vendor); VendorsService.createForUser throws ConflictException. Run this AFTER 04 Vendors > Apply to become a vendor in the same environment/run so {{accessToken}} already has a Vendor profile.

item.name: Ownership-guarded route fails closed on nonexistent id -> 403

request.description: Verified by reading source, not assumed: GET /api/products/:productId sits behind ProductOwnershipGuard. OwnershipService.isProductOwnedByVendor's own doc-comment states a nonexistent product id matches zero rows -- 'same fail-closed shape as not owned' -- deliberately, so this route can never be used to probe whether a given id exists. A real, authenticated, but non-owning caller therefore gets 403 here, not 404, even though the id genuinely does not exist.
